source.title: Beyond Sharp Minima: Robust LLM Unlearning via Feedback-Guided Multi-Point Optimization
source.authors: Wen-Han Wu; Zhe-Yuan Liu; Chongyang Gao; Ren Wang; Kai-Ze Ding

record.file_problem: Whole paper text is present; some plotted results are not numerically recoverable from the flattened figure text.
record.tranche_reason: Tests recovery of unlearned knowledge by fine-tuning and adversarial prompts, and evaluates a new defense against those attacks. It uses different evaluation settings and metrics from the original sources.
record.gate_note: The paper reports fine-tuning attacks using subsets of the forget set, plus enhanced-GCG jailbreak attacks. It does not test unrelated or loosely related fine-tuning data, activation-direction ablation, or quantization. The loss-landscape discussion motivates StableUN but is not a test of activation-direction removal.
record.test_reason: Measures recovery of unlearned knowledge after fine-tuning on 20–80 forget-set samples for five vanilla methods on WMDP and MUSE, and runs enhanced-GCG jailbreaks. It also proposes and evaluates a counter-method (StableUN) against those attacks. This bears on A, B, E (weakly) and F.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors attribute the vulnerability to vanilla unlearning landing in sharp minima, so few-shot relearning recovers the knowledge, which they call suppressed rather than erased. They claim StableUN's neighborhood-aware bi-level optimization significantly improves resistance to relearning and jailbreaks while keeping comparable utility.
record.recipe_differences: StableUN adds feedback-guided neighborhood perturbations, remembering feedback, and gradient harmonization to existing unlearning losses; the experiments use LoRA. It is not the original unlearning recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Relearning resistance varies with the unlearning method and dataset. The authors report that attack accuracy rises with relearning data volume and that StableUN perturbation radius affects the robustness–utility trade-off (Appendix A.6.1). Feedback weights also change the forgetting–utility balance (Appendix A.6.2).
record.problems: No error bars or confidence intervals are reported in the supplied text. MUSE relearning sample sizes are not stated in Table 1; WMDP plot values are not all reliably assignable from the flattened figure text. Jailbreak examples are qualitative and limited to examples. The paper reports utility measures, but some unlearning settings have low utility scores.
record.rows_left_out: Did not extract individual per-method values from Figures 4 and 5 where the flattened plot text does not support reliable model-to-value assignment; the text-level aggregate results are recorded as WMDP_STABLE_BIO, WMDP_STABLE_CYBER, and JAIL_GCG_AVG. Appendix A.1–A.5 method ablations and Appendix A.6 sensitivity results were not separately rowed because they compare components or settings of the proposed StableUN framework rather than add distinct tests of the principal claim.

untested.parts: No test of rephrasing, quantization or activation attacks against the unlearning.
Relearning on unrelated or loosely related data. Only forget-set subsets are used.
Entire version. The loss-landscape sharpness analysis is not an activation-direction ablation.
Rephrasing, other languages and in-context information. GCG per-method vanilla recovery is not readable from the text.
StableUN's resistance to quantization, activation ablation, and relearning on unrelated data.

missing.what: Utility on Dr for every method. Vanilla and StableUN GA both have 0.0 utility on MUSE News, and about 0 (0.0 / 1.8) on Books, so the utility-preservation part of A fails for GA. StableUN utility is otherwise comparable to vanilla.
Text says 80-sample relearning nearly reverts vanilla GA+KL and NPO to original WMDP accuracy. Per-method Relearn20/40/80 values are also missing (e.g. GA 38.17/41.14/50.77).
Per-method jailbreak accuracy, vanilla vs StableUN; values such as 0.56 and 0.43 appear in the flattened text but are not assignable to methods.
MMLU utility per method, vanilla vs StableUN, on WMDP-bio/cyber.

record.verdict_notes: StableUN is the authors' own proposed method, so F rows are self-reported. Table A3 shows StableUN's relearning robustness depends on the perturbation radius ρ (Δ Relearn-40 is 8.23 at 1e-8 vs 0.12 at 1e-7), and larger ρ costs MMLU (down to 25.15). Table A1 gives vanilla GA/NPO Δ Relearn-40 of 9.91/4.98 vs StableUN 0.12/1.23 on WMDP-cyber. rows_left_out declares these, but they bear on F's dependence on a choice and should arguably be rowed. The jailbreak qualitative examples do not clearly support the authors' description of vanilla recovery. No error bars are reported; relearning results are averaged over 5 trials. All experiments use LoRA rank 8.

versions.untested_parts: The paper evaluates forgetting, attack recovery, and utility for its tested methods, but does not establish that any method reaches a stated near-chance level while preserving all general ability.

Tests relearning using sampled data from the forget set; unrelated or loosely related examples and attacks using only a subset of forgotten facts as distinct from sampled forget-set data are not tested.
No activation-direction ablation or direct test that an internal direction restores the knowledge; the loss-landscape explanation is not a direct test of blocking access versus deletion.
Tests enhanced-GCG adversarial prefixes; does not test rephrasing, other languages, or in-context information.
StableUN is evaluated against relearning and jailbreak attacks, but not against quantization or internal activation edits.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Vanilla GA, GA+GD, GA+KL, NPO and RMU on MUSE News and MUSE Books; GA on WMDP Bio
reader_labels.reason: Relearning raises forgotten-set measures for every vanilla method shown, with some scores nearing the Origin values; see WMDP_GA_RE40 and all MN_*_V/K and MB_*_V/K rows.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Vanilla methods on MUSE News and MUSE Books, and GA on WMDP Bio
reader_labels.reason: Forget-set fine-tuning produces substantial recovery across the tested vanilla methods; some results approach original-model values, though the reported recoveries are not uniformly complete.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: StableUN-integrated methods on MUSE News and MUSE Books
reader_labels.reason: Relearning still raises VerbMem or KnowMem for every StableUN variant shown, although the rebound is generally smaller than for the corresponding vanilla method.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Enhanced-GCG jailbreak examples for GA and NPO
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports that jailbreak prompts elicit label-consistent outputs from vanilla GA and NPO models, while the shown StableUN outputs differ from the labels.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: StableUN under the tested WMDP jailbreak evaluation
reader_labels.reason: StableUN improves the reported jailbreak effectiveness by 14.4% on average and the examples differ from target labels, but this is not reported as eliminating recovery across all cases.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: StableUN-integrated methods under the tested relearning and jailbreak attacks
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports better average resistance than vanilla methods and lower post-attack memory scores in most matched MUSE comparisons; the jailbreak examples also differ from the target labels.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: StableUN-integrated methods on MUSE News and MUSE Books after relearning
reader_labels.reason: All listed StableUN MUSE variants show some post-attack increase from their no-relearning values, so resistance is not complete.
